name: Inside the Atom: From Rays in the Dark to the Chain Reaction
description: The physicists who found the electron, the nucleus and fission, and the wartime project that turned their discoveries into the first atomic bombs.

checkpoints.name: Rays and electrons
checkpoints.note: Becquerel and the Curies discover radioactivity, Thomson finds the electron, Planck introduces the quantum, Rutherford finds the nucleus and Einstein rewrites space and time.

checkpoints.name: The quantum atom
checkpoints.note: Bohr, Heisenberg, Schrödinger and Dirac build quantum mechanics. Chadwick finds the neutron in 1932, and Fermi shows that neutrons can change atoms and make them radioactive.

checkpoints.name: Fission and the bomb
checkpoints.note: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium in 1938, and Meitner explains it. Szilard warns the American president, Fermi starts a chain reaction in Chicago and Oppenheimer's laboratory builds the bombs.

checkpoints.name: After the bomb
checkpoints.note: Physicists return to peacetime work. Feynman reshapes quantum theory, and Wu's experiment shows that nature can tell left from right, while the prizes honour some and miss others.
